updates.description: End-to-end process automation with minimal manual intervention.

Automated, AI-powered data pipelines—from acquisition to dissemination—reduce manual effort, increase speed and quality, and enable real-time responsiveness across all stages of the statistical business process.
Employee input focuses on higher value work, innovation, and interpretation, not execution.
Surveys as a last resort, not first response.
Exploiting existing data holdings is the first response for new/existing data needs.
Admin data and alternative data is the second response for new/existing data needs.
Surveys are only used if necessary and are optimized dynamically based on cost-benefit analysis.
Designing, rendering and fielding a questionnaire is done using AI and takes no more than X time.
Searchable, usable, actionable data assets.
All data and metadata are standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable—built for interoperability and reuse across tools, systems, and organizations.
Discovery, understanding, and use are seamless for all types of users—whether human or machine—through APIs, metadata tagging, and open formats.
Our data ecosystem empowers internal and external users to find, consume, and transform data into new insights, products, and services.
Modular, reusable architecture and tools & services.
The organization has modular tools and microservices to increase agility, maintainability, and reuse across programs.
Business areas are empowered to prototype and develop smart solutions using supported self-service environments, with guardrails and shared libraries.
Open-source tools are the default, and employees openly share their code.
A modern, insight-driven workforce.
Analysts and researchers focus on value-add insight, not operational tasks—spending more time understanding context, building relationships, and generating actionable analysis.
Teams are curious, agile, and versatile—fluent in open-source tools, data science methods, and collaborative problem-solving across disciplines.
Analysts work in multidisciplinary teams that integrate design, technology, and subject matter expertise to deliver user-centered solutions.
Decisions are made by clearly designated owners—not by group consensus—but they are communicated and understood by those affected.
By 2030, Process (GSBPM 5.0) will operate infrastructure leveraging AI, ML, and advanced technologies to provide programs with rules for their Data Pipelines.
Resilient, auditable, and adaptive workflows will produce timely, trustworthy, and reproducible statistical outputs across all subject-matter areas.
GSBPM 5 sub-processes are orchestrated in modular, event-driven frameworks that are automated and version-controlled by design.
Analysts are no longer required to manually intervene, clean or manipulate files.
AI-enabled modules handle 50% of manual interventions for activities such as classification, edits and imputation for administrative and survey data.
Every processing pipeline is auditable, reproducible, and deployable across subject-matter domains.
Meta-data driven and standardization are default by design.
Data processing turnaround time has reduced by 50% across survey programs through automation and orchestration.
Microservices are used to manage each processing function (e.g. integrate data, edit, derive new variables, aggregate), with clear input/output standards across surveys and subject-matter areas.
Culture change: emphasis on the need for the right people to handle technical aspects and the importance of standardizing data formats.
Data integration: focus on facilitating integration, with architecture and FAIR principles playing a key role.
Self-service platforms and tools should make data pipelines transparent and user-friendly.
Create role-based training for orchestration and automation (pipeline creation, usage and maintenance).
Embed knowledge-sharing practices (community of practice).
Redefine roles and responsibilities: centralized versus decentralized systems, modular approaches, and standardization.
Agile governance: current governance structure is rigid, risk averse and slow for iterative digital innovation.
Real-time access to validate data supports faster insights.
Automated, reusable components reduce duplication.
Version-controlled workflows provide traceability.
Uniformity in data processing enhances reliability.
Reproducible pipelines reduce process errors and streamline analytical operations.
Transparent and systematic quality monitoring boosts data user confidence.
By 2030, the Analyse (GSBPM 6.0) process will be modernized where analysts focus on delivering high-value outputs by leveraging their analytical expertise and subject matter knowledge.
The Analyse process will use orchestration and embed technology (AI and automation) throughout.
Support an event-driven creation of outputs, validation, user-friendly and robust disclosure control, and preparation of tables and reports for dissemination in a timely way.
Analysts focus on value-added outputs such as interpretation and contextualization.
Reproducible, standardized analytical pipelines are the norm.
Publication preparation time is reduced by 50% leveraging AI and automation to facilitate output creation (e.g. Daily text) or validation.
Disclosure control outputs turnaround time is reduced by 50%.
FAIR-aligned data discovery platform enables better access and reuse.
A searchable, metadata-driven data discovery platform is available to all analysts, enabling them to easily locate and access appropriate data sources.
Implement AI-supported pipelines for auto-generated descriptive and exploratory analysis including daily write-ups, dashboards, and standardized analytical products.
Build infrastructure and tooling that enable real-time analytical workflows with intelligent validation and anomaly detection.
Use metadata repositories and FAIR standards for optimal integration into analytical pipelines.
Standardize pipelines with embedded validation rules.
Implement AI frameworks and ethical review processes to ensure human oversight, fairness, and trust in automated analysis.
Redesign the Analysis 101 curriculum to proactively meet modern analytical profiles.
Develop a unified, searchable metadata-supported platform to find and access the best available data for analytical questions.
Orchestrated and automated workflows accelerate end-to-end analysis providing relevant outputs faster.
Built-in validation, traceability, and cross-disciplinary input improve analytical robustness.
FAIR-aligned data platforms make it easier to find, access, and use relevant data sources for confrontation.
Automation and standardization reduce manual labour and operational overhead.
Integrated workflows foster innovation, cross-functional teamwork, and faster uptake of new methods.
Increased reuse and cross-functional application of existing data store.

Business Development is defined as a program where employees outside of IT (programs, methodology, operations) are enabled to develop solutions using approved low-code/no-code platforms and/or approved sets of tools within IT supported, security assessed, AI-enabled business platforms.
"Business Development" replaces the concept of "Citizen Development" (TBS).
Business Development is bound to the same security postures and digital guardrails as the usual software development – business development life cycle.
Business Development is an important and necessary role for the Agency.
Primary Data Collection business development: prototyping and exploration with business utilities.
Once reached the operationalization stage, use corporate development to ensure operational rigor, repeatability, stability and support.
Primary Data Collection business development includes paradata research and analysis.
Primary Data Collection business development includes business process automation through established platforms - PowerApps, RPA etc.
Primary Data Collection business development includes AI-enabled solutions within corporate AI environments/platforms/tools.
Secondary Data Collection (alternative data sources) business development serves as entry point for processing and analytical pipelines.
Business development for secondary data collection will follow patterns established for processing/analysis – including AI enablement.
Develop data cleaning and transformation tools that handle inconsistencies across different data formats and sources.
Leverage scalable computing resources that can quickly process large datasets.
Provide tools for rapid iteration of models.
Develop AI models for classification and other purposes and perform advanced analytics.
Develop methodologic algorithms and statistical models.
Support high code use cases and machine learning.
Build and deploy data analytics solutions for oneself or others, following the Standard on Managing Data Analytics Solutions.
Develop code, libraries, applications, etc. related to processing, modeling, visualization and analysis in statistical and administrative programs.
Provide a low-code/no-code platform with intuitive interfaces for data manipulation, orchestration and visualization.
Provide modern R and Python development tools like RStudio and VS Code that allow debugging, unit testing, etc. to improve code quality and productivity.
Integrate data from all sources and generate accurate, timely reports, to provide reliable insights that guide strategic decisions.
Run and support applications and pipeline built by others.
Provide data integration tools that can connect to both legacy and modern systems.
Create automated reporting pipelines that update data visualizations and dashboards in real-time.
Provide capability to perform manual edits.
Mostly done by IT: develop corporate solutions and enterprise grade platforms that are monitored, maintained, and supported through SLAs.
Mostly done by IT: create enabling infrastructure (networking, AVDs, security monitoring, etc.).
Mostly done by IT: create web applications or highly complex systems/data analytics solutions using cloud technologies and cloud native platforms.
Mostly done by IT: create applications or systems that impact multiple business areas, including mission critical programs.
Mostly done by IT: follow corporate guidelines, policies, directives and SDLC practices.
Mostly done by IT: follow SA&A process.

Business development: develop data analytics solutions (business logic) within IT supported, security assessed, AI-enabled production platforms (the Zone, Fabric) while following the Standard on Managing Data Analytics Solutions.
Business development: create data pipelines, R/Python scripts, modules and packages, visualizations and dashboards including use of AI methods.
Business development: create data edit/capture interfaces within security assessed platforms to allow for manual edits and overrides.
Business development: business process automation through established platforms - PowerApps, RPA etc.
Business development: only allow access to what the user needs access to.
Business development: follow corporate guidelines, policies, directives and Statistical Reproducible Framework practices - Data Analytics Solution development process.
Preparation of dissemination outputs: dissemination vision calls for a set of rules what dissemination outputs should be created for the website – using corporate tools.
Production of dissemination outputs will be the last step in the data pipelines.
Programs/operations will use activity groups for processing/analysis, including retrieval of external data for confrontation.
Processing/analysis activity groups will also be used to produce custom tabulations - design, certification, and production.
PUMP creation will be done with the use of corporate tools and business development will use processing/analysis activity groups if custom PUMF production is required.
Programs/operations will use corporate platform/toolkits to create and post outputs on the website – e.g., Drupal toolkit to create and post pages; data visualization platforms such as PowerBI.
Disseminating outputs for AI consumption: use corporate platforms to publish statistical data in format expected by AI bots/search engines.
Mission-critical dissemination processes – e.g., posting market moving data using embargo – will be done through platforms developed and maintained by IT.
